They are dignified landscapes with a tranquil, protected atmosphere. Faced with mounting casualties during the nation’s Civil War, Congress passed legislation in 1867 that authorized the creation of national cemeteries. Today, the National Park Service manages 14 national cemeteries, including some of the oldest national cemeteries in the nation. They are cared for as historic designed landscapes and as places of commemoration and respect for the fallen and their families. All are welcome to experience these hallowed grounds. Polynesians were well established on the islands when, about 800 years ago, Polynesians from the Society Islands arrived in Hawai`i. Claiming descent from the greatest gods, they became the new rulers of Hawai`i. After a time of voyaging back and forth between the Society Islands and the Hawaiian Archipelago, contact with southern Polynesia ceased.
